title: Sunny — 3yo canary: eating well but wasting away
presentation: 3-year-old male canary, losing weight over six weeks despite a good appetite, with a prominent keel and undigested seed in the droppings. Two other birds in the aviary have died in the same period.

stages.title: Examine the bird and the aviary
stages.briefing: Weight 16 g, down from 22 g. Keel prominent (BCS 1/5), pectoral muscle wasted. Fluffed up, sitting low on the perch. Droppings: loose, with whole seed visible. Vent slightly soiled. Aviary: mixed finches and canaries, seed and softfood, communal feeders, two deaths in six weeks, new birds added two months ago without quarantine.
stages.prompt: Which findings shape the differential list?

options.label: Weight loss with a good appetite and undigested seed in the droppings
options.detail: Maldigestion — the "going light" syndrome

options.label: Two other deaths in six weeks in the same aviary
options.detail: A transmissible process in the collection

options.label: New birds added without quarantine
options.detail: The likely route of introduction

options.label: Fluffed posture on a low perch
options.detail: Non-specific sign of illness in any bird

options.label: Soiled vent
options.detail: Follows the loose droppings

stages.explanation: Passerine keepers call this "going light" and it is a syndrome, not a diagnosis: weight loss on a good appetite with undigested food points at the proventriculus and gizzard. What turns it into an aviary problem is the mortality pattern and the unquarantined introductions — the plan will be about the collection as much as this bird.

stages.title: Choose the tests
stages.briefing: The canary weighs 16 g, so sampling has to be chosen carefully. Two carcasses are in the freezer and one bird died this morning.

options.label: Wet-mount and Gram-stained faecal or crop cytology
options.detail: Macrorhabdus and yeasts are seen on a stained smear

options.label: Post-mortem of the fresh carcass with proventricular histopathology
options.detail: The organism sits at the isthmus, visible on histology

options.label: Faecal parasitology for coccidia and Atoxoplasma
options.detail: The other going-light agents in passerines

options.label: Faecal culture for Gram-negative overgrowth
options.detail: Secondary invaders and a treatment target

options.label: Crop swab microscopy for Trichomonas and Candida
options.detail: Cheap, immediate differentials

options.label: Serum biochemistry panel on this bird
options.detail: The blood volume is not justifiable in a 16 g patient

options.label: Whole-body radiographs as the first-line test
options.detail: Little to see in a maldigestion syndrome, and restraint carries risk

stages.explanation: In a 16 g bird the sample plan is the clinical skill: microscopy on droppings and crop, and a proper post-mortem on the bird that has already died, rather than bleeding the patient you are trying to save. Macrorhabdus needs looking for specifically — it is missed on a wet mount and shows up on a Gram stain as large rods at the isthmus.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: Gram-stained faecal smear: numerous large Gram-positive rods, 2 × 40 µm, consistent with Macrorhabdus ornithogaster. Crop wet mount: no Trichomonas, no Candida. Faecal parasitology: no coccidian oocysts, no Atoxoplasma. Culture: mixed Gram-negative overgrowth, Escherichia coli predominant. Post-mortem of the fresh bird: thickened proventricular-ventricular isthmus, histology shows the same organisms within the mucus layer with mucosal hyperplasia. Body condition emaciated with no fat stores.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do these results support?

options.label: Macrorhabdiosis (megabacteriosis) of the proventriculus
options.detail: Organism on smear and in the isthmus on histology

options.label: The aviary is affected, not just this bird
options.detail: The same lesion in a second bird that died

options.label: Gram-negative overgrowth is secondary
options.detail: Predictable on a damaged, hypochlorhydric gut

options.label: Coccidiosis and atoxoplasmosis are excluded
options.detail: No oocysts and no parasites on cytology

options.label: Trichomoniasis explains the weight loss
options.detail: Crop wet mount negative

options.label: This is simple seed-based malnutrition
options.detail: It does not produce a thickened isthmus full of organisms

stages.explanation: Seeing the organism is not enough on its own — Macrorhabdus can be carried by well birds — so the histology showing mucosal hyperplasia at the isthmus is what makes it the disease rather than a passenger. The negative results are what stop the aviary being treated for coccidiosis, which is the reflex diagnosis for going light.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: Large Gram-positive rods on faecal smear, the same organism with mucosal hyperplasia at the isthmus on histology, negative for Trichomonas, Candida, coccidia and Atoxoplasma, secondary Gram-negative overgrowth, two aviary deaths.

options.label: Macrorhabdiosis with secondary bacterial overgrowth, affecting the aviary
options.detail: The organism, its lesion and its spread

options.label: Coccidiosis
options.detail: No oocysts found

options.label: Trichomoniasis
options.detail: Crop microscopy negative

options.label: Avian gastric yeast carriage without disease
options.detail: Contradicted by the mucosal hyperplasia and the deaths

options.label: Seed-based malnutrition
options.detail: Does not explain the proventricular lesion or the mortality

stages.explanation: Because the diagnosis is aviary-wide, so is the treatment: amphotericin B for affected birds, whole-collection management, hygiene of communal feeders, and a quarantine policy for new arrivals — which is the fault that let it in. Treating one canary and returning it to the same aviary is a guaranteed relapse.
